preregistered_hypotheses.H1: Per-primitive capability profiles of S1/S2/S3 are materially heterogeneous (primitive x model interaction != additive); no model dominates all 32 primitives.
preregistered_hypotheses.H2: A nontrivial fraction of chat-protocol failures is structural/protocol-induced (EMPTY_OUTPUT, INVALID_OUTPUT, format mismatch) rather than semantic INCORRECT; these are separable at trial level.
preregistered_hypotheses.H3: Harness adapters shift primitive-level accuracy non-uniformly across cognitive families (positive transfer on some, negative on others); a uniform all-family gain is NOT expected.
preregistered_hypotheses.H4: Local llama.cpp GGUF paired adapter contrasts directionally reproduce published native-harness improvements for at least the Pi adapter; magnitudes differ with quantization/runtime.
preregistered_hypotheses.H5: Adapter gains show partial cross-harness retention strictly below 1 on average (harness-specific interaction patterns learned).
preregistered_hypotheses.H6: Runtime intervention x adapter interaction (S3-S2-S1+S0) is nonzero for tool-mediated primitives; co-design adds benefit beyond additive effects only if CIs exclude zero.
preregistered_hypotheses.H7: Learnability classes (0/8, 1-7/8, 8/8 success) partition dev tasks; a material subset of 0/8 failures is protocol/runtime-addressable rather than capability absence.
preregistered_hypotheses.H8: The accuracy-vs-latency/tokens Pareto frontier admits no single dominant configuration across all axes; the best trade-off depends on workload family.
